steps.title: Registration authorities
steps.body: Registration Authorities lists the registration authorities (DMS) of the instance. Each one defines how devices are admitted and which CA signs their identities.

steps.title: Create a registration authority
steps.body: A DMS configures admission and the identity lifecycle for its devices. It acts as the registration authority; the CA you select signs the certificates.

steps.title: Name and ID
steps.body: The ID is derived from the name (DMS Showcase becomes dms-showcase). EST endpoint URLs use this ID, not the display name.
steps.note: The ID cannot be changed later, so choose a recognizable name before creating.

steps.title: Registration mode
steps.body: Just-in-time provisioning creates unknown devices automatically on their first enrollment. Pre-registration only lets devices registered beforehand enroll.
steps.note: Review Provisioning strategies before choosing for a fleet.

steps.title: Enrollment CA
steps.body: The enrollment CA signs the identities that devices obtain. Pick an active CA with a usable key and an explicit profile suitable for end-entity certificates.
steps.note: Keep the certificate CN compatible with the Device ID.

steps.title: Choose the enrollment CA
steps.body: In the example, DMS Enrollment CA signs the device identities. The test certificate should allow its intended use and expire within the issuer's validity.

steps.title: Validation CAs
steps.body: Validation CAs are the CAs trusted to validate the initial credential a device presents when it first enrolls (the bootstrap credential). They are distinct from the CA that signs the final identity.

steps.title: Choose the bootstrap CA
steps.body: DMS Bootstrap CA validates the initial credential. Add only the CAs you really trust for admission.
steps.note: Trust distribution is configured separately: it is not installed automatically.

steps.title: Create and verify
steps.body: Creating the DMS does not prove that authentication and issuance work. After saving, read the configuration again, query /cacerts and test one allowed and one rejected enrollment, then inspect the device, serial and history.
